title: US charges two Canadians accused of hacking US universities
content_md: A federal grand jury indicted two Canadians suspected of hacking multiple US universities and using the compromised systems to mine for cryptocurrency. 35-year-old Ryan James Roach and 41-year-old Mathiew James Stubbings now face a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison and a $250,000 fine each if found guilty of conspiracy to obtain information from a protected computer and to cause damage to a protected computer, obtaining information from a protected computer, and intentionally damaging a protected computer. According to court documents, the two accomplices used virtual private servers in multiple countries (registered under fake names) between June 2016 and December 2019 to infect systems on the networks of multiple unnamed educational institutions in New York, Tennessee, North Carolina, and Massachusetts with malware. "These servers transmitted malware and mining software to victim computers and stored stolen login credentials," the Department of Justice (DOJ) said. Once inside the victims' networks, Roach and Stubbings allegedly stole data and login credentials, deployed crypto-mining malware, and, in some cases, used compromised systems for vulnerability research after gaining access to supercomputers on the victims' networks.
